extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a benchmark designed to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations across 102 languages from 10+ language families, covering four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and speech retrieval across 3 speech domains.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson
extraction.inLanguage: 102 languages (including Afrikaans, Amharic, Arabic, Armenian, Assamese, Asturian, Azerbaijani, Belarusian, Bengali, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Burmese, Cantonese, Catalan, Cebuano, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Filipino, Finnish, French, Fula, Galician, Ganda, Georgian, German, Greek, Gujarati, Hausa, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Icelandic, Igbo, Indonesian, Irish, Italian, Japanese, Javanese, Kabuverdianu, Kamba, Kannada, Kazakh, Khmer, Korean, Kyrgyz, Lao, Latvian, Lingala, Lithuanian, Luo, Luxembourgish, Macedonian, Malay, Malayalam, Maltese, Mandarin, Maori, Marathi, Mongolian, Nepali, Northern Sotho, Norwegian, Nyanja, Occitan, Oriya, Oromo, Pashto, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Punjabi, Romanian, Russian, Serbian, Shona, Sindhi, Slovak, Slovenian, Somali, Sorani Kurdish, Spanish, Swahili, Swedish, Tajik, Tamil, Telugu, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Umbundu, Urdu, Uzbek, Vietnamese, Welsh, Wolof, Xhosa, Yoruba, Zulu)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S combines several public datasets (Multilingual LibriSpeech, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, MINDS-14) with a newly collected speech dataset named Fleurs, where between one and three recordings were collected for each of the 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets across 102 languages.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: FLEURS is a dataset that is complete at more than 97%. Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Audio recordings from LibriVox read audiobooks (MLS), European Parliament session debates (VoxPopuli), Common Voice, spoken examples from the e-banking domain (MINDS-14), FLoRes sentences read by speakers (Fleurs), and candidate text from Wikipedia and CommonCrawl.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Fleurs, new train-dev-test splits with 1509, 150, and 350 sentences were built with disjoint speakers between train and dev/test sets. For MLS, the official 10-hour splits were used. For VoxPopuli, 14 languages with more than 10 hours of data from the ASR task were used. For MINDS-14, monolingual sets were merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split. For speech retrieval, the pool of transcription candidates was augmented with 100k sentences from Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are taken from existing benchmarks (ASR transcripts, speech translations into English, 14 intent categories in e-banking, and language labels) and read-prompt text matching from FLoRes for Fleurs.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Between one and three recordings for each sentence (2.3 on average) for Fleurs.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets in Fleurs.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Updates will be made on the Hugging Face platform; slight improvements and replacements of low-quality recordings are planned for a second version.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation and catalyze research in universal speech representations, helping give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Performance discrepancies exist across geographical groups: baseline results are substantially higher on Western European languages compared to Sub-Saharan African or South Asian languages due in part to larger amounts of available unlabeled data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects relevant to speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated. Speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting given the discrepancy between input signal richness and the small number of output labels.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking, fine-tuning, and evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations on speech recognition, speech-to-text translation, speech classification (language identification, intent classification), and speech retrieval.
